thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — GPU-serving queue spiked above 1.2k and error budget breach approaching. Autoscaler attempted nodegroup create but failed. Marking SEV2 until mitigations confirmed.

oncall-sanjay: Ack, I'm on it. Checking autoscaler logs and ASG requests now.

olivia-platform: Seen the alert too. Quick note: affected cluster is prod-gpu-usw2, GPU pool name = gpu-pool-v2, recent LT rollout last night.

infra-marco: grabbing asg events -> looks like AttachRole error on instance profile for the new launchTemplate version. ASG API returned 403 for AttachInstanceProfile. Could be instance-profile name mismatch.

oncall-sanjay: kubectl get pods -n inference shows jobs piling in Pending with reason "Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" and queue length in our metrics dashboard spike 00:03 UTC.

katie-support: Customers reporting inference timeouts and 503s. Support ticket volume up ~45% for accounts on the dedicated tier. Need ETA for mitigation and any customer-facing guidance.

olivia-platform: Extract from autoscaler controller logs (recent):
```
E0423 23:05:12.123 autoscaler.go:422] NodeGroup create failed: error creating nodegroup: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform this operation
   status code: 403, request id: a1b2c3d4
Caused by: iam:PassRole denied for arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-gpu-instance-role
```

infra-marco: Confirmed. IAM role associated with the launch template (lt-0abc1234) references an instance role that was renamed in the infra change last night. ASG can't attach the profile.

oncall-sanjay: That explains failed node launches. Autoscaler kept retrying and we exhausted pool capacity. Manual scale doesn't help if attach fails.

incident-bot: @oncall-sanjay you have 15m escalation window before paging infra-sre.

oncall-sanjay: Taking next steps: 1) Temporarily revert LT to previous version that uses the older working instance-profile 2) Or attach a permissive temp profile to ASG via console 3) Evict taints / allow CPU fallback for low-priority jobs. Trying revert now.

olivia-platform: Revert attempt: updating ASG to use LT version 4 (previous). Command:
```bash
aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-pool-v2-asg --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abc1234,Version=4
```

infra-marco: Warning — version 4 had a different SG change; double-check SG rules (port 22 & metrics). But okay for short window.

oncall-sanjay: Applied update. ASG accepted the change. Watching new instance launches.

ops-bot: DeployBot: fired event - 2364111305 - ASG update applied by oncall-sanjay.

oncall-sanjay: New instances are starting. kubelet begins join, taints are applied; however, one node failed to register with kubelet due to incompatible kernel module (nvidia driver) mismatch. Logs show DKMS module build error.

olivia-platform: That's separate but manageable — we have spare LT that boots with preinstalled driver image (lt-0abc1234:v4-driver). Switching to that variant for the next batch.

oncall-sanjay: After swapping to driver image variant, 3 nodes joined and GPU resources now reported by Kubernetes. Pending queue dropped from 1.2k -> 180 over 7 minutes. API error rate down by 60%.

katie-support: Noted stabilization. I'll post a short status update to affected customers: "We've applied a config rollback and are seeing requests return to normal. Some jobs remain queued; full recovery expected in ~30m. We'll follow up with root cause."

infra-marco: Root cause summary so far: launch template rollout referenced a renamed instance profile (infra change). Autoscaler retries were masked as 'scale attempts' but underlying IAM attach failed. Secondary failure: driver image mismatch slowed node join.

oncall-sanjay: Mitigations performed: 
- Reverted ASG to LT v4 that had working instance profile
- Switched launch template variant to prebuilt driver image (v4-driver)
- Increased ASG desired temporarily by +6 to drain queue faster
- Marked low-priority batch jobs to allow CPU fallback where feasible
- Opened infra PR to fix instance-profile reference and prevent future rollouts without gating IAM changes

incident-bot: Paging infra-sre for postmortem and IAM policy review (escalation window hit).

olivia-platform: I'll own the follow-up PR to lock LT changes behind a pre-deploy check that validates instance-profile existence and passRole permissions.

katie-support: Socialization notes for comms: affected timeframe 23:05–23:25 UTC, ~20 minutes of elevated errors, estimated 4800 requests impacted, top 3 customers saw degraded latency > 10s. Draft message ready, will time with infra confirmation.

infra-marco: Action items: 
- Patch CI to run iam:PassRole dry-run for LT changes (olivia)
- Add autoscaler metric for 'failed attach attempts' so we alert earlier (marco)
- Add playbook step to try LT rollback before paging (sanjay)

oncall-sanjay: Closing on-call loop — system stable, queue draining, will hand to infra-sre and postmortem owners. If we see re-escalation, reopen.

incident-bot: Incident set to RESOLVED -> MONITORING. Postmortem required, assign to olivia-platform + infra-marco.

katie-support: Thanks team. I'll update support tickets and post a customer-facing note once PR merged.

olivia-platform: Adding initial postmortem notes to docs repo: cause, timeline, mitigation, follow-ups.

oncall-sanjay: Final check: metrics look green, autoscaler healthy, ASG stable. Leaving logs and kube events attached to the incident thread.

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: create follow-up RFC and add iam:PassRole check to preflight.

katie-support: Closing thread for now — will reopen if any regression. :white_check_mark:
